# Evaluating ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

I'll use integration by parts twice.

**First integration by parts:** Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)*dx
Then du = -sin(x)*dx, v = exp(x)

I = exp(x)*cos(x) - ∫ exp(x)*(-sin(x))*dx
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫ exp(x)*sin(x)*dx

**Second integration by parts** (for ∫ exp(x)*sin(x)*dx): Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)*dx
Then du = cos(x)*dx, v = exp(x)

∫ exp(x)*sin(x)*dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)*cos(x)*dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - I

**Combine:**

I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - I

2*I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)

I = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C

**Verification:** d/dx [exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2] = exp(x)*(cos(x)+sin(x))/2 + exp(x)*(-sin(x)+cos(x))/2 = exp(x)*cos(x) ✓

<answer>exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C</answer>
